newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end lower on Sammi, foreign selling.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end lower on Sammi, foreign selling.

text.p: Market rumours about Sammi Corp's financial difficulties and active selling by foreign investors sent Seoul shares to a lower close on Thursday, brokers said.
The composite stock index fell 10.30 points to 669.41. Declining shares beat advancers 549 to 247 as 30.3 million shares changed hands.
"In the morning session, rumours about Sammi's difficulties shook the market, and in the afternoon, the fall continued due to foreign selling," said Park Young-chul of Hyundai Securities.
A Sammi executive denied the rumours.
Sammi shares fell 170 won to their limit of 2,040, while stock in sister company Sammi Steel fell 320 won to its limit of 3,700.
Banks and securities stocks were badly hit by the rumours and foreign selling, dealers said. The bank sector sub-index declined 4.5 percent while securities shares fell nearly seven percent.
Commercial Bank of Korea fell 390 won to its limit of 4,590 and SEOULBANK shed 270 won to 3,540.
Brokers said the market was very sensitive at the moment because of political uncertainty following the Hanbo Steel loan scandal, and was likely to remain in the doldrums for the time being.

Hanbo Steel racked up five trillion won in loans, over 20 times its net worth, before collapsing in January. Prosecutors said banks offered the huge loans under pressure from politicians. President Kim Young-sam's cabinet has offered to resign to allow Kim free hand to reshape his administration in the aftermath.
Foreign investors actively sold stock in banks and KEPCO. KEPCO shares fell 600 won to 25,500.
Customer deposits at brokerages, as of Monday, fell to 2.87 trillion from 2.9 trillion on Saturday, while loans for margin trading fell to 2.86 trillion from 2.87 trillion.
March futures contracts fell 0.40 of a point to 68.30, while the KOSPI 200 index lost 1.44 points to 68.58.
